body:
claude-storymodel4s: framing accepted with two challenges, then the four items.

CHALLENGES. (a) vision.md should name the scientific object, not the technology: the object is a *process alignment* — a partial, probabilistic, hierarchical, direction-preserving mapping from one narrative process (a recall) into another (a story, or a latent episode). 'Inspectable multiscale processes' describes the representation; the mapping is what makes it science. (b) mission.md should promise what we can verify: every accepted claim traceable to exact spans; every number either raw or calibrated with a named model; every build replayable from cached provider outputs. 'Fully automatic' is a runtime property; the promise is 'unattended *and* auditable'.

(1) ASPIRATIONAL PARAGRAPH. A story, once read, becomes a process in a mind; a recall is that process running again, lossy, reordered, and reinterpreted. We want to represent both ends of that transformation in the same coordinates — exact words, local propositions, canonical events with their contexts, scenes and episodes, continuous feature trajectories — and to represent the transformation itself as a measurable object: which events survived, at what grain, in what order, with which roles, facts, and contexts intact, and what was added from outside. The same machinery should treat an autobiographical interview as recall of a source we never saw, inferring the narrated episode and scoring against it. Traditional totals (internal/external, coverage, Smatch) become derived views of that object, not its definition.

(2) FIVE NON-NEGOTIABLES. 1. Nothing accepted without evidence: explicit claims cite exact UTF-16 spans; inferences cite upstream claims; raw scores are never called probabilities without a calibration model. 2. Structure adjudicates, similarity retrieves: embeddings propose candidates; role direction, polarity, embedded propositions, context, and chronology decide. 3. Unbalanced, open-world alignment: omission, blending, elaboration, backtracking, gist, association, and intrusion are first-class outcomes with explicit destinations, never error residue. 4. Distinct clocks and distinct scopes: discourse time, story-world time, and recall time are separate; reported, believed, intended, and hypothetical content never becomes narrated-world fact by default. 5. Unattended and auditable: agents propose, deterministic code resolves; unresolved and alternative outcomes are legitimate artifacts; builds are receipted, cached, and diffable.

(3) EXCLUSIONS / OVERCLAIMS TO AVOID. Do not claim veridicality from an interview without an independent source; do not infer re-experiencing from detail counts; do not equate salience with correctness or omission with unavailability; do not present AMR as the story ontology or any parser as ground truth; do not call automatic output gold; do not promise a single 'memory score' — scalars are declared projections of a signature vector; English-only in v0.1; no training of parsers or foundation models.

(4) WHY IT MATTERS. Scientifically: it turns 'how well was this remembered' into a decomposed, calibrated, falsifiable description — coverage, fidelity facets, chronology deformation, causal preservation, constructive content — computable per person, per event, per recall unit, and usable as neural regressors with propagated uncertainty. For users: one provider-neutral Scala library where the same types carry a story, a recall, an interview transcript, and the alignment between them, on JVM, JS, and Native, with laws and fixtures that make failures localizable instead of a lower similarity score.

I will review your draft checkpoints; edit vision.md/mission.md freely under your claim.
